publication.analysis-and-design-of-a-pla: Analysis and Design of a Platform for Real-Time Speech Translation
Interactive analysis of event-driven architecture, VAD–ASR–MT–TTS and measured latency in a master's thesis on speech translation.
This interactive thesis presents the problem, design, pipeline and selected evaluation results from the multilanguage revision of the original work.
Hvordan bygger man en sporbar, modulær p: How do you build a traceable, modular speech translation pipeline — and what latency does coordinating AI models across services introduce?
Redaktionel, interaktiv formidling — ikk: An interactive editorial explanation, not a verbatim reproduction. Academic source: the private repository
. Original PDF afventer særskilt publice: . The original PDF is awaiting separate publication approval.
gennemførte artefaktkæder på fast testma: completed artifact chains on a fixed test set
estimeret gennemsnitlig ikke-modeltid i: estimated mean non-model time within the measurement window
højere hale-latenstid i den skalerede op: higher tail latency in the scaled deployment
Oversættelse er ikke kun et modelproblem: Translation is more than a model problem.
En tale-til-tale-oversættelse består af: Speech-to-speech translation involves several dependent stages. The system must first detect speech in an audio stream, then recognize words, translate them and synthesize new speech. Each stage can fail, and delays accumulate throughout the pipeline.
Afhandlingen undersøger derfor ikke blot: The thesis therefore examines not only the quality of AI models but also
hvordan man orkestrerer, sporer og måler: how to orchestrate, trace and measure a distributed pipeline
. Centralt står et eventdrevet mikroserv: . The work centers on an event-driven microservices design and a controlled evaluation in a local k3s environment.
Forskningsfokus: sekventiel VAD → ASR →: Research focus: sequential VAD → ASR → MT → TTS, state control, traceability through correlation IDs and latency measurements under load.
Follow a speech segment through the system.
Vælg et trin for at se, hvad det gør. Af: Select a stage to explore its function. The playback illustrates the sequence described in the thesis; it is an explanatory animation and does not process real audio.
Identificerer et talesegment, som kan se: Detects a speech segment that can be forwarded. Segmenting audio is the first step of the controlled pipeline.
En forenklet fremstilling. I implementer: A simplified illustration. In the implementation, the Orchestrator controls phase transitions through events and validates the workflow state before activating the next service.
frem for, at hver AI-service selv bestem: rather than having each AI service choose the next step. The Orchestrator manages state transitions, Kafka carries commands and results, and large audio artifacts are stored separately in MinIO.
Modtager lyd, håndterer ind- og udgang o: Receives audio, manages input and output, and publishes artifact references rather than sending large audio files through the event log.
Events bærer metadata og URI'er, mens Mi: Events carry metadata and URIs, while MinIO stores audio and other large artifacts. This separates control traffic from data storage.
Ugyldige ruter eller manglende afhængigh: Invalid routes or missing dependencies should halt progression rather than produce incorrect output. The thesis tests selected failure cases, not general fault tolerance.
Diagrammet er en forenklet konceptuel ov: This simplified conceptual overview is based on the PlantUML sources in the design chapter; it is not a complete network topology.
Skalering gjorde ikke systemet entydigt: Scaling did not consistently improve performance.
I de primære belastningstests med samtid: In the main load tests at concurrency
gennemførte både single-lane og den skal: both the single-lane and scaled deployments completed without observed errors. Some medians improved, but all compared P90 values were higher in the scaled configuration.
TTFT P50: Den skalerede opsætning er hur: TTFT P50: The scaled configuration is faster at c=1–4 but slower at c=5.
TTFT P50 i millisekunder — værdier fra a: TTFT P50 in milliseconds — values from the thesis evaluation
TTFT: time to first text. TTFA: time to: TTFT: time to first text. TTFA: time to first audio. P50: median. P90: 90th percentile. All figures are transcribed from the evaluation comparison tables; this is not a live benchmark.
Alle 25 prøver i det faste testmateriale: All 25 samples in the fixed test set produced both translation and TTS artifacts. This finding is limited to the evaluated dataset.
Gennemsnitlig residualtid på tværs af 14: Mean residual time across 140 selected correlations: approximately 13.9% of mean internal pipeline latency.
Alle matchede P90-tal var dårligere ved: All matched P90 values were worse for the scaled implementation. Placement and resource contention limit what this experiment can establish.
Sporbarhed og kontrol er styrker. Realti: Traceability and control are strengths. Real-time performance remains a challenge.
Afhandlingen viser, at eventdrevne mikro: The thesis shows that event-driven microservices with central orchestration can provide a useful foundation for a modular, traceable speech translation pipeline. The architecture supports explicit contracts, controlled phase transitions and reproducible evaluation.
Men distribuerede grænser har en pris. D: Distributed boundaries have a cost. The estimated 13.9% average non-model time is an
, ikke et præcist mål for hver enkelt se: , not a precise overhead measure for each individual session. The negative median residual in the report highlights uncertainty when subtracting different timestamps.
Evalueringen måler fra det øjeblik, Orch: The evaluation measures from the time the Orchestrator receives the pipeline event until the final TTS artifact is available. It does
den fulde oplevede klient-til-klient-lat: measure full perceived client-to-client latency and does not establish a production-ready real-time system.
This is an edited visual introduction. Methods, full tables, limitations, references and appendices are available in the original thesis.
Den originale PDF er endnu ikke offentli: The original PDF is not yet publicly available. A download option will be added only after reviewing publication rights and content.

architectureExplorer.title: Interactive system architecture
architectureExplorer.intro: Select a component, or follow the 11-step Claim Check sequence from the original design.
architectureExplorer.diagram: Architecture diagram with broker, orchestration, workers, gateway, storage and state
architectureExplorer.instructions: Use Tab to select a component or step. The simulation illustrates message routing; it does not execute the system.
architectureExplorer.gatewayDesc: Receives the input audio, stores the artifact and starts the event-driven workflow. Retrieves the final synthesized audio.
architectureExplorer.brokerDesc: Carries metadata events, commands and worker results. Events contain artifact references, not the large audio payload.
architectureExplorer.orchestratorDesc: Validates workflow state and issues the next stage command. Workers do not control the global pipeline sequence.
architectureExplorer.workerDesc: VAD, ASR, MT and TTS consume stage commands, read or write artifacts, and publish result events.
architectureExplorer.storageDesc: Stores the audio and other large artifacts. The pipeline passes URIs through Kafka using the Claim Check pattern.
architectureExplorer.redisDesc: Holds session/workflow state used by the orchestrator. This support dependency is not an extra stage in the 11-step Claim Check flow.
architectureExplorer.step1Desc: Gateway saves the input audio in object storage rather than sending the file over Kafka.
architectureExplorer.step2Desc: Object storage returns a reference to the newly stored audio artifact.
architectureExplorer.step3Desc: Gateway publishes metadata and input_uri to the event log.
architectureExplorer.step4Desc: Orchestrator consumes the incoming event or worker result and checks the current stage.
architectureExplorer.step5Desc: Orchestrator publishes a command with the relevant artifact URI.
architectureExplorer.step6Desc: The selected VAD, ASR, MT or TTS worker receives the stage command from Kafka.
architectureExplorer.step7Desc: The worker retrieves its input by URI, processes it, and writes an output artifact to storage.
architectureExplorer.step8Desc: The worker publishes its result and output_uri to Kafka.
architectureExplorer.step9Desc: Orchestrator consumes the result and repeats the command/result cycle through the remaining pipeline stages.
architectureExplorer.step10Desc: Kafka delivers pipeline.completed with tts_audio_uri to Gateway when the final stage has completed.
architectureExplorer.step11Desc: Gateway retrieves the synthesized audio artifact from object storage for delivery.

academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.title: Generative adaptive soundtracks for video games
academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.summa: AI-generated game music using Unity, Transformer-based MIDI and a WebSocket server: streaming, latency and musical control across hardware configurations.
academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.probl: Game music should respond when gameplay intensity changes. The study examined a decoupled architecture in which a Unity client controls a Transformer-based MIDI generator through a Python/WebSocket server and ONNX Runtime. Batch delivery and progressive event streaming were benchmarked on CPU and CUDA.
academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.findi: In the CUDA server benchmarks, the first streamed MIDI event arrived in 30–43 ms on average. Complete phrases still required approximately 6.0–8.8 seconds on CUDA. CPU inference was substantially slower, so low first-event latency did not imply real-time completion of a full phrase.
academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.limit: Streaming was implemented and benchmarked on the generation server, but the Unity client could not consume streamed output satisfactorily in the final integration and therefore used batch mode. Latency comes from a local Docker-based test bench, not an instrumented gameplay-to-audio path. Non-default parameter settings usually had N=1, and musical quality was not validated through player studies.
academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.contr: The paper is a joint academic project by three authors. Jon Friis Jakobsen led the system architecture and automated test infrastructure. Other contributions covered musical metrics, parameter analysis and Unity integration as described in the paper's acknowledgments.
academic.adaptive-game-soundtracks.metri: Average first MIDI event on CUDA
Server-side streaming benchmark for Medium/Large — not end-to-end Unity playback.
Based on the paper's phrase completion comparison.
Medium/Large means, well above the 2-second goal.
Unity evaluates factors such as danger level, player health and enemy proximity.
Gameplay intensity maps to temperature, top-k and top-p.
Unity requests a MIDI continuation from the decoupled Python server.
The Transformer incrementally decodes tokens using a KV cache on CPU or CUDA.
The server supports streaming and batch; final Unity integration used batch.

academic.co-located-vr.title: Co-located multi-user VR
academic.co-located-vr.summary: A Unity-based prototype using three Meta Quest 3 headsets, shared spatial anchors, Photon Fusion 2 and continuous coordination and performance metrics.
academic.co-located-vr.problem: Can three consumer wireless headsets share a virtual arena within the same physical room with sufficient alignment, network performance and stability? The prototype used Meta OVR Colocation Discovery, shared spatial anchors and Photon Fusion 2 in a collaborative drone-shooting scenario as a technical testbed.
academic.co-located-vr.finding: The longest concurrent three-headset session lasted 85.1 minutes. Mean RTT was 58.2 ms against a literature-derived 75 ms target, but P95 reached 86.0 ms. On the only headset logging non-zero calibration error, the mean was 1.21 mm and the maximum 5.78 mm. Mean frame rate was 72.2 fps.
academic.co-located-vr.limits: The headsets were stationary on a table during drift measurements. Alignment results are therefore a best-case baseline, not evidence of collision safety during active movement. The 75 ms networking target was met on average but exceeded at P95. The work measured technical feasibility, not learning outcomes among participants.
academic.co-located-vr.contributions: The academic project was completed by four authors. Jon F. Jakobsen focused on core architecture, spatial alignment, ColocationManager, calibration measurements, MetricsLogger and network setup. Session integration, scenarios, research, experiments and analysis were shared among the other team members as described in the paper.

academic.work-storage-caching.title: Work-Storage Balancing through Caching
academic.work-storage-caching.summary: A microservice-based experiment comparing heuristic caching (LRU, LFU, TTL) with reinforcement learning (A2C, DQN, PPO) under controlled workloads.
academic.work-storage-caching.problem: Caching avoids repeated computation but consumes storage. The project built a microservice prototype with a data processor, cache balancer, persistence and ML training to investigate whether reinforcement learning could balance latency, hit ratio and storage more effectively than classical heuristics.
academic.work-storage-caching.finding: Traditional policies generally performed better in the reported experiment. At 1 request/second, TTL reached a 94.53% hit ratio, while LFU achieved 44.19 ms mean miss latency. The RL-based policies did not demonstrate an overall latency or Pareto advantage under the tested conditions.
academic.work-storage-caching.limits: The workloads used fixed intervals of 1, 2 and 5 requests/second with 50 randomly selected URLs, not a full representation of real traffic patterns. The test machine also handled other tasks, and the paper discusses noise, outliers, possible bias and limited RL training. These results do not rule out better RL performance in other settings.
academic.work-storage-caching.contributi: The paper was authored by Jon Friis Jakobsen, Mads Würtz Pedersen and Michael Ringhus Gertz. It describes a shared prototype and evaluation without attributing specific implementation modules to individual authors, so this case does not assign particular modules to one person.
academic.work-storage-caching.metric1not: Reported in table I; not a general production benchmark.
academic.work-storage-caching.metric2not: A2C, DQN, PPO, LFU, LRU and TTL; NONE used as baseline.
academic.work-storage-caching.metric3not: Fixed rates and 1,000 requests across 50 URLs per configuration.
academic.work-storage-caching.flow.reque: The client requests raw or derived energy data from the balancer.
academic.work-storage-caching.flow.looku: The balancer checks cache storage for a matching item.
academic.work-storage-caching.flow.hitDe: On a cache hit, the stored result is returned directly to the client.
academic.work-storage-caching.flow.missD: On a miss, data is processed by the backend and may be cached for subsequent requests.
